title: Volume 2 Chapter 3: Howling for You Who Cannot Cry 4
content: I had indeed killed the Goat Demon Tribe.
It wasn't because I had confirmed it by severing its head or anything like that.
I was certain because I had witnessed with my own eyes the magical power disappearing from the Goat Demon.
Having just been attacked by that Horse Demon Tribe with their high regeneration abilities, I was not careless.
However, I had to admit that I had made a mistake.
Unlike monsters, the corpses of demons do not turn into magic stones or magic stone fragments upon death.
Instead, they crumbled and bubbled as they disintegrated.
And from the melting corpse, I could see a sphere.
I had to acknowledge that I had made a fatal mistake.
As the flesh literally bubbled and magic power leaked into the atmosphere with each pop, it was being absorbed into the half-dead sphere that should have been the size of a human fist.
No, that thing was not a corpse.
It was still alive, and it continued to pour out its magical power.
As long as it was alive, it was impossible to prevent the magic power from leaking out.
But if that sphere existed, the situation changed.
Once that sphere was activated, it would greedily absorb the surrounding magical power.
The Goat Demon had made the decision to throw away its life the moment its head was severed.
I didn't know if it retained consciousness, but I had underestimated its determination.
And I had underestimated the length of their hands and their meticulousness.
"Why is something like that here?"
Erika, the Erika Solnzali, was in shock.
But her moment of shock was short-lived.
With the sound of the Great Demon Knight's magic stone fragment being drained of magic power and shattering, we sprang into action.
I suddenly recalled words taught to me at the academy.
I think it was a male teacher with white hair who had passed middle age.
His face was one that would likely not be seen in the Faltarl Kingdom, which had maintained peace for many years, as if he were joking.
"If you see that on the battlefield, turn around and run away with all your might.
You won't be shamed or scolded; in fact, you'll be praised, as long as you survive."
I had thought he was a teacher who made jokes that weren't funny, but I never expected to experience it years later.
No, it's really not funny.
Just before I turned my back, I felt as if the head of the Goat Demon lying on the ground had laughed.
"W-What!? What is happening!?"
Shara, who was being carried in a princess carry by Erika, shouted in confusion.
We were running away now.
With all our might.
"Because there was something bad," Erika said regretfully.
"There was something very bad."
"What do you mean by something bad?"
Erika hesitated to answer Shara's question, likely because of her noble upbringing.
Among nobles, there is this idea that war is the job of nobles.
Commoners need not concern themselves with war, nor do they need to know the pride and foolishness that comes with it.
It's an arrogant thought.
If you unravel history a bit, it's common for commoners to get caught up in wars, so it's ridiculous.
But perhaps this is a thought that comes from me having strayed from the proper path of nobility early on.
So I answered in Erika's stead.
"It's a magical tool, the worst kind of magical tool."
Shara looked at me, silently asking what kind of magical tool it was.
"Some idiot, specifically a fool named Rainibati, created a magical tool meant to blow up cities."
Its name is
"Rainibati No. 5,
" the fifth magical tool created by the madman Rainibati, who established peace on the continent for the past hundred years.
Magic is a mimicry of divine works, skills are miracles bestowed by the gods, and magical tools are the crystallization of human wisdom.
A madman who wished to study magical tools in a world without war spread the crystallization of wisdom across the world.
It proves that human wisdom is not always used for good.
"A magical tool that blows up cities? That can't be!"
Shara swallowed her words of disbelief, perhaps because she saw my face or Erika's.
"It exists, and in large quantities across various countries."
I suppressed the urge to shout about the meaning of such a thing appearing before us.
I couldn't help but smile wryly at my own forced cheerfulness.
"If everyone had such things, there wouldn't be any wars, right?
That's what the idiot who created and spread them thought."
"W-What kind of idiot would do that?"
Shara shouted, expressing a perfectly valid question.
"That would be Rainibati from the Faltarl Kingdom, and just so you know, he died over a hundred years ago."
"Is there only idiots in Faltarl?"
I thought she had casually included us in that insult, but I let it slide.
I understood that it was her way of easing her fear.
"So do we have a chance of surviving?"
Shara's question was directed at Erika, not me.
Her voice was incredibly calm.
It wasn't resignation; it was the words of someone who had accepted their fate.
As expected, she was the woman who had tried to fight the Golden Ogre to buy time for villagers to escape, even with bones protruding from her abdomen.
Her quick thinking was on par with us adventurers.
Erika's next words were as steady as ever, and I had to admit it was likely thanks to Shara's calm demeanor.
"I'm sorry, Shara. To be honest, I don't know.
If we weren't in the forest, I could guarantee we would escape beyond the range."
That's right; we couldn't run at full speed in the dense forest of the Demon Realm.
To make matters worse, we were in the Demon Realm.
A "dense" wave of magical power passed through us, pushing us forward.
In the Demon Realm, Rainibati No. 5 would have no shortage of magical power to absorb.
After all, the forest of the Demon Realm itself was a phenomenon close to a type of magic.
Once Rainibati No. 5 absorbed a certain amount of magical power, it would start emitting waves of magical power.
The range of these waves was meant to signal impending death.
So please run away; that was the madman's good intention, or so it seemed.
These waves would gradually narrow in interval and, in the end, would reach a speed akin to the heartbeat after running, at which point the magical tool would activate.
What a tasteless form of good intention.
I gritted my teeth at the unexpectedly rapid release of magical power waves.
At this rate, we probably wouldn't be able to escape.
For a brief moment, Erika's magical power, influenced by the wave behind us, wavered and then became taut.
"Shin, please take care of Shara."
Without even glancing back at me, Erika threw Shara into the air.
I caught Shara, who was screaming, "No way!" with both hands.
I couldn't help but click my tongue at the fact that my first experience with a princess carry was with Shara.
Shara shouted, "What was that tongue click for?" but I ignored her for now.
Erika's golden magical power flickered like flames as it rose.
"I will create a path."
Her back told a story beyond her words.
"Please keep the Solnzali secret technique a secret."
Despite her joking tone, her back eloquently conveyed her refusal to give up, no matter the situation.
In an instant, Erika's red hair ignited.
I could tell Shara in my arms held her breath, so I knew it wasn't just my imagination.
In the next moment, an immense amount of magical power gathered in Erika's hands.
Erika had been surprising me all day.
The concentrated golden magical power in her hands looked to me like a crystal made of gold.
I could only react to Erika suddenly stopping in her tracks because I was certain that stepping in front of her would mean certain death.
Erika exhaled a short breath.
I couldn't accurately put into words what happened next.
Because I didn't understand what had occurred.
As a phenomenon, I could explain it.
A magic I had never seen before, comparable to the ancient dragon's breath, was unleashed from Erika's hands.
As a result, a new path suddenly appeared in the forest.
Flames scattered from Erika's blazing hair, and as she said,
"I'm going,
" she took off running, leaving me to follow her uncertainly.
"Two hours, no, at least three hours of chant-class power..."
Shara sighed in my arms.
"Are there any normal people in Faltarl?"
Shara, who was likely a chant magic user capable of doing something comparable to Erika, said this with a stunned expression.
She could probably grasp the absurdity of what Erika had just done.
"Of course there are."
I said this with a deliberately bright voice because I felt a sense of dread from Shara's tone.
Seeing Shara like that reminded me of my classmates when we talked about Erika at the academy.
For some reason, I didn't want Shara to look at Erika like they did.
"Specifically, that would be me."
I was met with Shara's half-lidded gaze.
"Are you seriously saying Erika's husband is normal?"
Hmm, that's true.
A person who could become Erika's husband couldn't possibly be normal.
In the eyes of the world, such a person would be called the luckiest man alive.
So I corrected myself honestly.
"Indeed, I was the luckiest man in the world to have become Erika's husband."
I intended to make a serious correction, but Shara covered her face with her hands and shouted,
"This couple!
This couple is like this!
Then Erika unleashed the Solnzali secret technique twice more, and we found ourselves in a hole.
Yes, a hole.
To be precise, we found the church in the Demon Realm, which should have been standing for over sixty years, just as we were about to reach our original destination.
We decided to bet on the church's sturdiness.
Erika created a hole using magic, shielding us within it.
The intervals of the magical power waves had become quite short, and if Rainibati had been weak, we would have already reached the heartbeat after running.
In other words, it could explode at any moment.
That was one of the reasons we had dug a hole in the ground.
The other reason was,
"I'm sorry, if only I had a bit more magical power..."
Sweat beaded on her forehead as Erika spoke, her breath ragged.
If Erika Solnzali had a bit more magical power, it would be in the realm of myth or legend, I thought, shaking my head.
"You've done enough, Erika.
With the trees of the Demon Realm and the church that has endured for sixty years, wanting anything more to serve as a shield would be greed.
I looked at Erika's hair, which had turned as white as ash.
Her red hair had turned white in several strands.
It seemed that the Solnzali secret technique she had used drained her immense magical power and demanded the price of her beautiful red hair turning white.
After digging a hole in the ground with magic, Erika had exhausted all her magical power.
Choosing to hide by digging a hole was more because her magical power was running low than because we had found the church.
Finding the church was merely a coincidence.
After all, we hadn't even confirmed the direction we were fleeing in.
I entrusted Shara with Erika, who could barely stand, and leaned out of the hole.
"Where are you going?"
I was genuinely surprised by the anxious tone in Erika's voice as she called out to me.
I even doubted if it was an auditory hallucination.
That voice reminded me of my childhood.
When I struggled to use magic properly and trained recklessly, I recalled the moment I had
"used up
" my magical power for the first time.
That feeling of having exhausted my magical power brought a unique sense of anxiety and insecurity.
It felt as if nothing in my body was certain, floating on dark and unstable waters.
As a child, I had cried out for help from my father and mother.
Erika was likely experiencing that feeling for the first time in her life.
Having exhausted her innate immense magical power was not something she would have experienced being born and raised in the royal capital.
"I'll go find a lid to cover the hole."
I almost blurted out that I wouldn't go anywhere, but I bit my tongue.
"I'll be back soon."
I spoke a bit quickly, feeling embarrassed because of Erika's weak appearance, which I had never seen before.
I almost found meaning in her unspoken wish for me to stay close, to not leave her side.
When I glanced back one last time, I saw Shara with a face resembling a human stuffed with sugar.
I emerged from the hole I had dug a little distance away to avoid being caught in the church's collapse.
In the dense forest, the church stood out with its artificial straight lines, its walls darkened over sixty years but retaining its original shape.
Compared to the other buildings around it, which had mostly left only traces, it was clear that it had been built with the determination of those who had established the frontier of the Demon Realm.
I silently offered a prayer.
This place had been the forefront of the Demon Realm's development, and at the same time, it was an ancient battlefield.
Sixty years ago, it was the site where many adventurers fought and died against a monster known as the
"Eight-Legged Three-Armed Swordfoot.
That was why I was sure I would find something I was looking for.
"I'm back."
It was a narrow hole, so it was obvious I had returned, but I couldn't help but say it when I saw Erika lying at the bottom of the hole.
The intervals of the magical power waves were already as fast as the heartbeat after running, and it could explode at any moment.
In Erika's stead, Shara asked me,
"Um... is that the lid you mentioned?"
It had only been a minute since I left the hole, so naturally, Erika's magical power had not recovered.
I couldn't tell if she was breathing lightly because she knew it would help her recover faster or if it was instinctual.
Personally, I felt it was the latter.
No, I had learned this at the academy.
I could easily recall Erika's appearance from our academy days.
While remembering Erika during the breathing exercises in our magical power recovery class, I answered,
"Yes, it's a large shield that someone used sixty years ago."
As I responded to Shara's question, I pulled out the large shield that was half-buried in the ground and lightly tapped it.
It was likely a fine piece crafted by a master using good materials, as it had not rusted or decayed after sixty years and retained its former appearance.
I positioned the shield on my back, large enough to easily conceal a person, to cover Erika and Shara.
I took out a rope from the tool pouch that had miraculously not been blown away during the battle with the Great Demon Knight and secured the shield to my body.
Thank goodness, I was able to enhance my body like I did with my sword.
Now all that was left was to wait for the explosion when Shara spoke up.
"When is this going to explode?"
Her bright tone was likely a sign of her concern for me.
I averted my gaze from the Sister, who was calmly hiding in the hole while waiting for a magical tool that could blow up a city to activate, and answered,
"They say it will explode when the intervals of the magical power waves reach the speed of a heartbeat after running."
In response to my answer, Shara said with a laugh, "If it were my heart, it would have exploded a long time ago."
I thought,
"Is there only dangerous women around me besides Erika?
" while increasing the strength of my body enhancement in preparation for the explosion.
I wondered if I could adjust it properly and spoke carefully to avoid my voice turning into a high-pitched squeak.
I had to be careful since Erika couldn't use body enhancement right now.
"It seems Rainibati was surprisingly good at physical activities.
Even my heart could explode at any moment."
"Weren't we taught in class that Rainibati was an excellent warrior in his lifetime?"
It seemed my attempt to convey this to Erika backfired.
"Well, I can guess what you were doing during class."
Her voice held a hint of exasperation.
"Yeah, I was mostly looking at you during class."
"You're not good at lying, Shin."
Even though I spoke honestly, she denied it for some reason.
More importantly, she knew I had been looking at her, right?
No, it seemed I was being perceived as an irresponsible student.
"Well, I was an irresponsible student."
I replied with a wry smile, and Erika hesitated for a moment before apologizing.
"I'm sorry; I made you worry with that answer.
I apologize, Shin. Your goal might not be achievable."
Before I could ask what she meant by my goal, Erika continued,
"I truly regret involving Shara in my circumstances and causing this situation... Shara?"
When I looked at Shara, who had a puzzled expression while nibbling on dried meat, she tilted her head and said, "Huh?"
I inadvertently locked eyes with Erika.
The Erika Solnzali was silently conveying that she thought Shara was dangerous.
Well, I couldn't say for sure if she truly felt that way, but it was clear she was quite surprised, and I found myself serious in front of someone who stood alongside my master and junior disciple.
"N-No!"
Shara flailed her arms, looking at both me and Erika in a panic.
I felt a bit relieved when I saw the church, and then I got a little hungry, so it's not like I was letting my guard down or anything!
I’m a Sister, you know! Being near the church makes me feel instinctively safe!"
A painful silence passed for about five beats of magical power, and then Erika began to chuckle.
I couldn't help but laugh along.
I certainly wasn't trying to laugh to cover up the fear of this crazy Sister.
"Well, yes, yes. I suppose I was 'at fault' here.
Apologizing isn't really my style, but even if this might be the last time, I should say it.
It has been a very enjoyable time, and I thank you both.
If possible, I would be grateful if you would continue to accompany me.
I quite like my current life and would love for it to continue."
Shara swallowed her dried meat and responded to Erika's words.
It doesn't feel like this is the end at all, and honestly, I'm a bit taken aback that you can say you had fun, but regrettably, I had fun too.
After she finished speaking, Erika and Shara looked at me with expectant eyes.
Did this mean they wanted me to say something too?
Well, if I thought it might be the last time, it would be easy to be honest.
"Since that day, there hasn't been a single day I haven't been happy since I got on that carriage."
Just being able to be by Erika's side, who continued to spew curses, made me happy.
I was delighted to stand next to Erika as she wielded her sword.
I was happy to envision myself in the near future she spoke of.
Hearing her worries, complaints, and little daily words brought me joy.
After throwing my life away, I found so much happiness packed into it; since that day I got on that carriage, I could say I was happy no matter when I died.
And—ah, that's right.
"Erika, let's live like this as long as you want.
It's a cute whim from my wife.
I'm a useless husband, but I'll do my best to fulfill it."
Just like that morning.
There is nothing cuter than my wife's whims, I smiled.
I didn't have anything that could compare to what you lost or what you should have gained.
The only thing I could offer was my meager life.
Still, I would be by your side when you laugh, rampage, unleash magic, and punch through the absurdity.
I would do my utmost to ensure Erika could be that way.
I genuinely believed that.
To convey that seriousness, I nodded at Erika.
Erika let out a sound that was more of a grunt than a word, while Shara covered her face with both hands and shouted,
"Read the room, damn it! Saying something only the two of you understand at a time like this!"
Then the magical power wave suddenly stopped pulsing, and I said, "Brace yourselves."
As the magical power wave that had been pressing against my eardrums ceased, it happened immediately.
I distinctly heard something shatter in the distance.
Shara said something, but I couldn't hear her voice; I understood that the space had shattered.
It wasn't logical.
With a smile, Shara was saying something to Erika and me.
Rather than being surprised, I felt bewildered by Shara's ability to smile and say something in this situation.
I unconsciously read her lips.
"Look—voice—Erika—it's—okay, God—"
Before Shara could finish her sentence, a shock hit me, shaking my head violently, and I gave up on reading her lips.
For a moment, I thought I heard a voice that wasn't Shara or Erika in the distance.
"May the blessing of the priestess's sword be upon you."
Now, about what happened after that.
To put it simply, we were completely unscathed.
I thought, "No way," but it was true, so there was no helping it.
Shara was excitedly shouting about the blessing of God.
In the barren wasteland of the Demon Realm, where not a single blade of grass grew, it was understandable to say that upon seeing the church standing unharmed.
In reality, it was likely because the barrier device installed in the church, in other words, the sacred artifact, detected us and activated the barrier.
That was Erika's impression as she felt her magical power being absorbed toward the church.
As a mere ordinary person, not a light priestess or anything, I found that much more understandable and convincing than Shara's claim of divine blessing.
What? You didn't hear that?
Well, the truths of the world are often difficult to comprehend.
I think it's a simple truth that if I have Erika's smile, I can do anything.
To be honest, a massive upheaval had occurred, blowing away part of the middle layer of the Demon Realm, and I wanted to retreat as soon as possible.
However, since Erika's magical power had not recovered, and our original goal was right in front of us, we decided to rest at the church for now.
While I could stand and walk, Erika was still severely exhausted, so I entrusted her to Shara and explored the church.
The interior was nothing special; it was an ordinary church, but the bishop's words,
"You will know the sacred artifact when you see it,
" turned out to be true.
I had no obligation to protect it, but the bishop had asked me to keep the sacred artifact confidential, so I remained silent about the details.
That much was acceptable.
After all, they had mistaken Shara for an assassin, so it wouldn't be a breach of duty to keep that from Erika.
I wouldn't forgive them for trying to execute Erika, though.
Ah, I digress.
After about an hour's rest, we left the church.
Looking back, it was a foolish thought, but I was walking with trepidation, wondering when I would encounter the corpse of an unrelated adventurer caught up in Rainibati No. 5.
It wasn't so much the corpse itself that bothered me, but rather how Erika's expression would cloud over upon seeing it.
As you know, such worries were unnecessary, as by the time we retreated from the middle layer, other adventurers were desperately fighting off the monsters that had overflowed from it.
This was also a result of the assassins dragging the Great Demon Knight out from the depths, so indirectly, it could be said to be our fault.
However, it was better to die fighting than to die caught up in Rainibati No. 5.
In the end, it seemed there were no casualties among the adventurers, and they likely earned more than usual, so they were probably quite happy.

By the time we emerged from the forest, we were instead defeating the monsters returning from the shallow layer, so in that sense, I wished the adventurers of Hekatai would work harder to hunt the monsters.
After all, Erika was happily unleashing magic, saying, "Look, my magical power has recovered quite a bit."
Just a moment ago, she had been completely drained of magical power, and Shara was astonished, if not exasperated, while I found myself worrying because I was still not fully recovered.
Eventually, when we emerged from the forest, the adventurers of Hekatai, who had been driving the monsters away, gasped and stepped back in surprise.
Well, I was grateful they cleared the path without unnecessary exchanges.
As for me, I was the only one who had purified my bloodied equipment with healing magic and returned home safely.
See? We didn't do anything wrong, did we?
So let's stop making such serious faces, shall we?
Right, senpai?
